McDonald’s International 
Management
By Carson, Sasha, Sylvie

Quick Service Restaurant (QSR) Global Analysis
●
North America dominates with 37.03% of market share
●
Growing due to changing consumer preferences
○
Healthier eating
○
Busier lifestyles
●
Increase in online ordering
○
Need for advanced online platforms

QSR European Analysis
●
Value of $168.47 Billion out of $1055.48 Billion globally (~16%)
●
Dependent on international tourist (100% increase since 
Covid-19)
●
2023- European Commission changed minimum wage 
regulations in Germany, France, and Spain
○
Challenge for QSRs
●
Urbanization trend increases demand for QSRs
●
Increase demand for globally driven flavors - “it’s a must” 
(Gregg Majewski, CEO of Craveworthy Brands)

Mission Statement
“Our mission is to make delicious feel-good 
moments easy for everyone.”
“Our mission is to make 
delicious feel-good moments 
easy for everyone.”

Competitive Advantages
●
Global Brand Recognition
○
over 40,000 locations in more than 100 countries
●
Franchising
○
95% of McDonald’s are franchised
○
Locally sourced
○
"three-legged stool": Franchisees, Suppliers, and McDonald's 
Business
●
Cost Leadership
○
maximize efﬁciency & minimize costs

International Strategy
●
Based in a “three-legged stool” 
approach
○
Franchisees
○
Suppliers
○
Mcdonald’s Businesses
●
Emphasis on franchising
○
80% worldwide are operated by 
small or mid-sized businessmen 
and women
●
Focus on adaptability and innovation
●
Went international in 1967 in Canada

Entry Strategies
●
Uses the Velocity Growth Plan (2017)
○
Retain, Regain, Convert
●
“Think Global, Act Local”
●
Employs various entry models for different 
situations
○
Licensing - Latin America
○
Joint Ventures - Japan
○
Wholly Owned Subsidiaries - France

●
Entry depends on various factors (Politics, Environment, Religion, etc…)
●
Not in countries like Afghanistan, Bhutan, Iran, Iraq, Libya, and North Korea
●
Ex. North Korea has a large disapproval of western culture

Implementation Strategy
●
Scalable and proﬁtable expansion 
model
●
Standardization and adaptability
○
Streamlines the process 
○
Allows McDonald’s to appeal to 
local tastes
○
Ex. offering spicy meals in 
Indonesia
●
Requires the Global Standards for 
Safe, Respectful and Inclusive 
Workplaces

●
Not getting stuck in the “one size ﬁts 
all” strategy
●
Pricing that does not align with 
competitors
●
Rigid supply chains that don’t 
comply with local laws and standards
●
Adapting to local market’s taste
●
Extensive research into the markets 
they are entering
●
Emphasis on supporting local 
industries
Failures
Successes
●
Test entry into new markets through 
entry methods like licensing
●
Adopt to more sustainability and 
healthier menu globally
●
Ensure food safety and cleanly 
protocols are enforced regularly
Recommendations
